item.title: FCC approves SpaceX to launch up to 1 million AI‑chip satellites under Starmind
item.description:
FCC approves SpaceX to launch up to 1 million AI‑chip satellites under Starmind

The FCC announced Wednesday that it has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million AI‑chip‑equipped satellites under the company’s Starmind initiative.

🔍 Overview

  • FCC approval for a full AI satellite constellation.
  • First such approval; Google and Blue Origin are also pursuing similar concepts.

🧩 How it works

  • Starmind will capture solar energy in space to power AI workloads on Earth.
  • Data will be sent to Earth via high‑speed lasers that link to the Starlink network.
  • Chips for the satellites will be produced at SpaceX’s upcoming Terafab facility.

⚙️ Key details

  • Deployment deadline: at least one satellite must be in orbit by 2033.
  • Full constellation target: 1 million satellites by 2040.
  • FCC deferred SpaceX’s request to use “graveyard” orbits above 600 km, citing insufficient disposal information.

🚀 Timeline & Competing Efforts

Company Project Recent development
SpaceX Starmind FCC approval; deployment schedule 2033‑2040
Google Project Suncatcher Launched its first AI server satellite last month
Blue Origin Project Suncatcher Will perform the first dedicated heavy‑lift launch for the project in 2029

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a regulatory pathway for large‑scale AI compute in orbit.
  • Could extend AI processing capacity while using solar power captured in space.

item.title: Google to Launch AI Processor Satellite via Project Suncatcher
item.description:
Google to Launch AI Processor Satellite via Project Suncatcher

Google is launching a satellite equipped with its AI processors on October 1st to test their performance in space. This mission is part of Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers into orbit.

⚙️ Key details

  • Launch Date: October 1st
  • Launch Vehicle: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket
  • Hardware: Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs)
  • Orbit: Low Earth orbit, where the satellite will harness the power of the sun

🔍 Overview

The goal of the mission is to measure how well TPUs “handle the physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space.” While Google found during testing that its TPUs can withstand radiation and high levels of g-force, the company notes that “some things can only be tested in space.”

🧩 How it works

Google is testing a cooling system using radiators and heat pipes while the chips are in orbit. According to Travis Beals, Project Suncatcher’s senior director of product management, the chips can only run for approximately 15 minutes before they must be turned off to cool down.

🚀 Availability

Following this initial launch, Google plans to put two satellites into orbit next year.
